subject: density estimates from multi sessions (aka study areas)

messages.author: 37ca2736ee34244e
messages.subject: density estimates from multi sessions (aka study areas)
parts:
Hi All,

I am Iding, currently doing camera trapping field work in a Sumatran rainforest. I have four study areas that each comprises of ~ paired camera trap stations. My aims is to estimate density of clouded leopard and further species interaction, temporal and spatial. 

I realized that although with enormous effort that doubled or even quadrupled, I found little capture and recapture of targeted animal: the Sumatran clouded leopard. I detected individuals 3-5, from each study areas. Encouragingly, I detected female cloudie in each study area (session) but not surprisingly, I got very few detection.

For the models, I have ran constant model that estimate cloudie density across study area as a single population. I therefore would like to focus on how to:
  1. estimate density of cloudie in each session as independent location as each has >60-80 km apart.
  2. include sex as covariate and see if density between male and female is different.
  3. estimate sex ratio considered that I have very limited female detection.
For the analyses, I have been assisted by Mike Meredith but the more I read, the more I am confused. 

I really appreciate if you could spare your time and thoughts on this matter. 

Cheers,
Iding

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: density estimates from multi sessions (aka study areas)
parts:
Dear Iding
Thanks for your enquiry. I hate to say this, but I do not think you can conduct a meaningful capture-recapture analysis of such a sparse dataset. I know there are many instances of capture-recapture methods being applied to very sparse datasets, but I think we have to be clear that this is undesirable. Your hard-won data may have to stand on their own without statistics, or at most provide a single pooled estimate of density.
Regards
Murray

Hi Murray,

Thank you, not really encouraging indeed. But I am feeling better as not only myself have very limited capture-recapture data esp. for clouded leopard. I'll try different approach then, that could be following your suggestion to perform single pooled density estimate.

Best regards,
Iding
